think_procedure: To determine if max_wal_size is a special knob, I need to analyze its behavior and possible values. The max_wal_size parameter in PostgreSQL controls the maximum size to which the WAL (Write-Ahead Log) can grow during automatic checkpoints. Let me examine its possible values: 1) It accepts positive integer values (in MB) that represent the actual maximum WAL size limit, 2) It has a special value of -1 which means 'unlimited' - when set to -1, PostgreSQL will not limit the WAL size based on this parameter, effectively disabling the size-based checkpoint triggering mechanism, 3) The value 0 is not valid for this parameter. Since -1 has a completely different semantic meaning (unlimited/disabled) compared to regular positive integer values (specific size limits), this breaks the natural numerical order and represents a special case.
